newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 5.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Money and forex markets are edgy over the reported plans to tax state titles and relaxed foreign exchange policies expected to be adopted by the Bank of Greece. Yesterday saw outflows of forex worth 300 Ecu and an upward trend in interbank rates as well as the drachma's slide against the Ecu.

--The final decisions on the government's economic policy will be taken today at the meeting between Prime Minister Costas Simitis and National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou. Simitis is expected to give his stamp of approval to the taxation of large real estate holdings and of state titles at the meeting.

--Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas briefs Simitis on a unified policy for the farm sector. Simitis approves Tzoumakas's plan to table an omnibus bill on a variety of problems affecting farmers and farming.

--Telecommunications Organisation (OTE) has placed its 1.144 billion drachma contract for renewal of its satellite system with Comsat RSI, represented in Greece by SPACE Hellas. --Greek railways (OSE) signs on joint UK-German-Austrian-Greek consortium 'Hellas Rail Consult' as project manager for its five-year investment programme.
IMERISIA

--Three Athens Stock Exchange member firms were barred from trading yesterday while another six have been warned to comply with the clearing house on delivery of shares. Brokerage circles said the treatment meted out to Nuntius and Delta was 'discriminatory' as the two firms were barred from trading shortly before the close.
--The banking market is nervous about yesterday's agreement between Papandoniou and Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos to tax derivatives.
--Athens Chamber calls on the government to immediately abolish the special environment tax imposed on firms involved in infrastructure projects.
KERDOS

--The expected taxation of state titles has led investors - mainly foreign - to act quickly to protect themselves from possible unpleasant developments. The major concern for investors is not the imminent taxation of state titles but the possible retroactive taxation of state titles.

--Bank of Greece warns about the cost of production, saying that if the government does not take this factor into account, the balance of payments deficit will continue to increase dangerously. The central bank recommends a strict incomes policy for both private and public sectors.
EXPRESS
--The finance ministry is considering a capital gains tax on transfers of over 51 percent of shares.
--Simitis has the new budget in his hands today but whether it will be discussed by ruling party PASOK bodies is still unanswered.
--The new framework for procurements for state organisations overseen by the transport and communications ministry the subjects of Simitis and Transport Minister Haris Kastanidis's meeting yesterday.
--Simitis will have to personally intervene to get the ball rolling on the issue of privatisations.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The markets give warning signs of the repurcussions of taxation on bonds and derivatives as capital flows out and interest rates rise.
--Moody's considers upgrading Greece's sovereign ceiling rating.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
